newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends down vs dlr, forward premia slip.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends down vs dlr, forward premia slip.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended Friday at 35.76/77, down from the day's opening quotes of 35.74/76, dealers said.
In active trade, the rupee hit a low of 35.79 on sustained corporate demand and buying from a large state-run bank before retracing partially, they said.
"The dollar was well bid throughout the day," a dealer said. "There was good dollar demand while supplies seemed to be a bit tight today."

In forwards, premia held steady for most of the day until a statement by Finance Minister Chidambaram that the government wanted interest rates to come down turned market sentiment bearish, dealers said.
"Premia came down from yesterday's closing level and bounced back on profit-taking," a dealer said. "But they still ended down from yesterday's close. The undertone is soft."
The premia for six-month dollars ended Friday at 10.79 percent against Thursday's close of 10.92 percent, dealers said. Banks in Bombay are closed on Monday for a local holiday.
